subject: Deployment mode follow-up: capacity / latency clarifications + next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode recommendation and next steps

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can land the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary from our call:
- Primary workload: appointment scheduling + triage prompts (low token per request, latency-sensitive).
- Baseline: ~120 req/s.
- Peak behavior: you mentioned periodic spikes during morning scheduling windows.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + PHI-sensitive data discussed; you flagged potential need for VPC controls.

Questions to confirm (short answers appreciated):
1) Is 120 req/s a sustained baseline per region, or an average across multiple regions?
2) For spikes, is 5x what you expect (i.e., ~600 req/s) or just short burst peaks (seconds vs minutes)?
3) Do you require a customer-managed VPC (Private deployment) for all production traffic, or would VPC peering to Dedicated be acceptable?

Initial thoughts: if your 120 req/s is sustained with 5x frequent spikes and a strict P95 latency target <200ms, Dedicated reserved capacity is likely the recommended path for predictable performance and an SLA. Hosted API can be great for early integration and lower startup cost, but it does not give the same capacity reservation guarantees or VPC isolation.

I attached the discovery notes from today for our records (discovery-notes.pdf). Once you confirm the three items above I’ll loop in engineering to produce a short capacity-sizing proposal and pricing band.

Best,

Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode recommendation and next steps

Camila —

Thanks for the recap, that aligns closely with what we discussed. Quick answers below:  

1) 120 req/s is our baseline target for the primary US-east region (we expect most traffic to be in US-east).
2) Spikes: planning assumption is up to 5x baseline for ~10-20 minute windows during business hours (scheduling batch windows). We also want graceful degradation rather than hard failures if spikes briefly exceed capacity.
3) Compliance: data is PHI-classified. We prefer a deployment that allows VPC peering or a private endpoint; full on-prem is not required initially but we need SOC 2 evidence and control plane isolation for production.

Procurement and legal want an initial estimated TCO and an SLA commitment for P95 latency. Can you provide a ballpark for both Hosted API and Dedicated options so we can compare internally? I attached a CSV with our expected hourly QPS distribution (expected-qps.csv).

Also looping procurement: procurement@acmehealth.com — they’ll own contract details.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T09:30:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: deployment mode recommendation and next steps

Hi team —

Thanks Maria — good data, that helps. Technical read (brief):

- Baseline 120 rps sustained in a single region with 5x (600 rps) 10–20 minute spikes and P95 < 200ms is at the edge of what multi-tenant Hosted API can reliably guarantee. Hosted is low-friction for integration and cost-effective at low steady-state, but it does not provide capacity reservations or a hard SLA for sustained high-throughput workloads.

- Recommended path: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) in US-east with autoscale headroom. Example configuration: 2x dedicated inference nodes sized for your model family + autoscale policy to add 1-2 nodes for spikes. That setup gives deterministic tail latency and operator-controlled autoscale cooldowns to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

- VPC / compliance: Dedicated supports private VPC peering for isolated egress and can be combined with our Private control plane option (if you later need an on-prem control plane). For SOC 2 evidence we can provide the standard compliance pack and audit artifacts during procurement.

- Optimizations to reduce cost/latency:
  * Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (can cut token work in half depending on reuse).
  * Moderate quantization if using large models (tradeoff: small quality delta for big perf gains).
  * Request-level batching (we can configure continuous batching with short latency windows to preserve P95 targets).

- Rough pricing bands (very approximate, for internal budgeting):
  * Hosted API: lower entry cost, estimated $Xk–$Yk/month at your baseline traffic (no capacity reservation).
  * Dedicated (reserved): higher committed cost, estimated $Yk–$Zk/month depending on node size and retention of warm cache.

Next recommended steps:
1) 45–60 minute capacity sizing workshop (we’ll bring runtime engineers) to validate node sizing and autoscale policies.
2) Pilot on Dedicated for 2–4 weeks with monitoring and SLAs enabled.
3) If VPC-only is required for production, we can scope VPC peering and any additional compliance steps in parallel with pilot.

I attached a short agenda for the sizing workshop (capacity-sizing-agenda.pdf). If you’re good with the plan, Camila — can you propose 2–3 slots for next week and we’ll run the sizing workshop?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
